central_question: Is money being held, withheld, overlooked or left unclaimed?
audience: US adults 25-65. Homeowners, employees, parents, consumers, travellers, accident victims, former tenants, people managing estates, people dealing with insurance or medical bills.

format.tone: Calm, credible, practical. No 'free money' language. Every episode ends with a verification step.

episode_structure.purpose: The programme, obligation, settlement, policy or legal mechanism.
Missed deadlines, missing documents, wrong assumptions, scams, incomplete submissions.
Official databases, notices, administrators, documentation. Named on screen, never in the description alone.

sign_off: The money may be unclaimed. It does not have to stay that way.

visual_style.style_string: Soft matte low-poly isometric 3D illustration, clean thirty degree isometric projection, pale sage green background, objects modelled in warm bone cream and pale putty with soft long diffuse shadows, cornflower periwinkle blue used for hands handles and human elements, one saturated emerald green accent used only to mark money that is recoverable, simple faceless rounded figures at consistent small scale, matte non-reflective surfaces, soft even ambient light with no harsh highlights, generous negative space around the subject, subtle film grain, no photorealism, no gloss, no textures, 16:9
visual_style.ground: Plain pale sage #D8E0D6. Objects float on plain sage with no floor plane, no room, no horizon unless the scene requires ground.
visual_style.accent: One saturated emerald green #3AAE5C, the single accent.
visual_style.accent_rule: Emerald marks money that is recoverable. Warm grey marks money that is gone. Emerald appears on exactly one object per frame. If the frame contains no recoverable money, it contains no emerald.
must_not_look_like: Gradients, reflections, neon, or a second accent colour

motion.rule: One action, one shot, roughly five seconds. If a beat needs two things to happen, it needs two clips or it needs a simpler idea.
permitted: An object depletes, empties, fills or drains
A single element draws on or is revealed
One item is lifted, placed, opened or closed
A slow drift or a very slow push, no more than a few percent of frame
A shutter, drawer, lid or door moves once
forbidden: anything that breaks the locked-off isometric
motion.composed_not_generated: Draw-on reveals, the accent landing last, arrows travelling along a money trail and any type animation are Hyperframes GSAP work, not clip prompts.

thumbnails.formula: One object plus one number or one eligibility trigger.

disclaimer_block: This video is general information, not legal, tax or financial advice. Eligibility, amounts and deadlines vary and change; nothing here guarantees a payment or outcome. Always verify through the official sources named in the video before acting. Links below go to official databases and administrators only.

shorts.source_beat: How to verify it (the 'how to check' beat)

rpm_estimate_usd: RPM $10-22, CPM $22-45. Higher on insurance, tax, banking, legal compensation; lower on general refunds.
